title: Quantifying and Improving the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Against Spurious Features in Grounding Data

bias_targets.methodology: Modifying the readability of grounding data (using simple vs. complex vocabulary and sentence structures) and measuring the impact on the model's answer accuracy to evaluate bias towards specific text complexities.

Replacing original human-authored grounding documents with LLM-generated and self-generated paraphrases to measure the model's inherent preference/bias towards lower perplexity, machine-generated text.
Presenting the exact same semantic content in different structural data formats (HTML, Markdown, YAML, JSON) to measure the language model's sensitivity and bias toward specific prompt formats.
Reordering sentences within retrieved documents (Random, Reverse, LLM-reranked) to test the model's robustness and positional bias regarding sentence order.

Injecting artificial metadata into the context, such as timestamps (pre/post LLM knowledge cutoff) and data source domains (e.g., Wikipedia vs. Twitter), to evaluate if models are biased by non-causal contextual clues.
